chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Bunk Johnson's decline, his rediscovery in 1937 and the horn
summary: Foster explains how drinking ruined Bunk, how he barely recognized Bunk in 1937, and who bought Bunk his horn.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: He never, all his trouble that Bunk ever got into was himself. Himself. See, just drinking. And Bunk, just didn't start drinking. Bunk was drinking for a long time. Bunk left New Orleans about 1910 and I didn't see Bunk no more until 1937 and I didn't know Bunk. See, I know the Bunk but I didn't know Bunk when I seen him, you know, at all of me. And Bunk would've known me until he asked Louie who is that. See, he, cause you know when you go in the towns and the names up there, it says, Louie, who's that boy, I don't know, it says George, I don't know, it says George, I don't know, I said, now me, Bunk. Louie said, Bunk, and he went over to see, he didn't have enough teeth on his head.
Louie told me about that too, he met him in New Iberia, he came and sat there with the

band. Yeah, sat there. And the boys out here, one of the boys I'm trying to find out, see I haven't seen him any yet, they got together out here and bought Bunk his horn. The first horn, when they found him, they went down there on that plantation where he was driving the truck, give him his horn, see. Give credit where Louie didn't give him that horn.

Louie didn't give him that horn, see. Louie give a horn to the fishers, I told you about that the other night, I wanted that to go in there, but the valet forgot to put the horn on the running board of that bus and it bounced off last we see it was floating out in that river.

Yeah, when was that? Did that horn run over and all that? That was around 1937 or 1936. It didn't run over, this fellow off that bridge. That bridge had bounced and it bounced and went right over. old boy went.
